adjudication_label: batch_7:Dislocation unlocking and stress-strain curve manifestations
canonical_question: How does the 'unlocking of aged dislocations' mechanism specifically manifest in the stress-strain curve shape beyond the simple load drop?

question_variants.question: How does the 'unlocking of aged dislocations' mechanism specifically manifest in the stress-strain curve shape beyond the simple load drop?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text references that type-C serration is known to occur due to unlocking of aged dislocations but does not describe how this manifests in the stress-strain curve beyond a load drop.

answers.answer: The text cites a general mechanism where type-C serration results from the unlocking of aged dislocations but does not elaborate on the specific curve shape manifestations beyond the load drop.
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific curve shape details beyond load drop not provided
evidence_spans: Figure 13 shows a scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Fig. 13a ), EDS mapping image (Fig. 13b ), and particle size distribution (Fig. 13c ) of the pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA powder.
The pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi powder had a spherical shape, and was confirmed to have an even distribution of Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, and Ni elements.
The average diameter of the initial powders was measured as 27.2 um ( d 10 = 17.9 µm, d 50 = 26.1 µm, d 90 = 38.2 µm).

source_evidence_spans: In general, type-C serration is known to commonly occur at high temperatures as a result of the unlocking of aged dislocations [63]
